scope: Flow and preinfusion interpretation for Decent espresso traces

knowledgePolicy.recorded: A value directly present in a machine or scale sample.
knowledgePolicy.derived: A deterministic calculation from recorded samples and their timestamps.
knowledgePolicy.inferred: A phase or comparison produced by an explicit rule and labelled as such.
knowledgePolicy.unknown: A physical or sensory claim that the available signals cannot establish.

sources.title: How the DE1 measures
sources.scope: DE1 display and pressure/flow measurement concepts
supports: pressure and flow are distinct plotted signals
flow and pressure curves describe machine behaviour
doesNotSupport: diagnosing channeling from a curve alone

sources.title: How to dial in D-Flow
sources.scope: D-Flow profile family and its fast-fill/pressurised preinfusion concept
supports: D-Flow uses profile phases and adaptive behaviour
fast fill and pressurised hold are profile intent
doesNotSupport: D-Flow is optimal for every coffee

sources.title: The impact of the preinfusion flow rate on espresso extraction
sources.scope: Decent DE1PRO experiment varying preinfusion flow while holding selected variables
supports: preinfusion flow can change peak pressure, yield and extraction metrics in the tested setup
doesNotSupport: transfer to every machine, basket or bean

sources.title: Influence of Flow Rate, Particle Size, and Temperature on Espresso Extraction Kinetics
sources.scope: Controlled extraction experiments and chemical component mass
supports: in the tested conditions higher flow reduced component mass

sources.title: Systematically Improving Espresso: Insights from Mathematical Modeling and Experiment
sources.scope: Model and experiments on dose, grind, pressure, flow and non-uniform extraction
doesNotSupport: a single flow curve guarantees uniform extraction

sources.title: Decent Espresso Profile Guide
sources.scope: Examples and intended use of pressure, flow and adaptive profiles
supports: profile intent can be flow-controlled, pressure-controlled or adaptive
grinder and roast context affect profile behaviour

sources.title: Extraction of espresso coffee by using gradient of temperature. Effect on physicochemical and sensorial characteristics of espresso
sources.scope: Espresso fixed and gradient brewing-temperature profiles for selected Arabica and Robusta coffees
supports: brewing-temperature profile can change chemical and sensory results in the tested setup
doesNotSupport: temperature advice independent of coffee, machine and profile

sources.title: Influence of serving temperature on flavour perception and release of Bourbon Caturra coffee
sources.scope: Serving temperature, volatile release and descriptive sensory evaluation for one coffee cultivar
supports: tasting temperature changes volatile release and perceived flavour attributes
doesNotSupport: transfer to every cultivar or serving context

sources.title: Impact of consumption temperature on sensory properties of hot brewed coffee
sources.scope: Descriptive sensory analysis of four hot brewed coffees consumed at 50, 60 and 70 °C
supports: coffee samples can respond differently to consumption temperature
doesNotSupport: a universal sensory direction for all beans

hardLimits: never equate machine flow with beverage mass flow
never claim channeling or extraction yield from pressure/flow alone
never hide missing or incompatible traces

temperaturePolicy.brewingTemperature: Machine/group temperature target or measured trajectory during extraction.
temperaturePolicy.tastingTemperature: Measured or user-entered beverage temperature at sensory evaluation; never inferred from machine telemetry.
temperaturePolicy.sensoryAdvice: Use temperature as a conditional controlled experiment only after matching or recording dose, profile, grind cohort, strength and tasting conditions.
temperaturePolicy.precision: Do not imply validated sensory precision below the resolution and uncertainty of the sensor and tasting protocol.
